$comment: STATIC COPY for the Team module. Stands in for GET /api/v1/admin/team/vocabularies. Labels, tones, help text and the transition table — permanent content, NOT placeholder records. The panel renders from this rather than hard-coding, so a status relabelled server-side needs no code edit. TONES ARE THE PANEL'S OWN SIX and no new colour is introduced: ok · warn · bad · info · brand · '' (neutral), plus `dead` for cancelled, which is the existing inset + line-through treatment. If a status here ever needs a colour that is not in that set, the status is wrong, not the palette.

attendanceStates.label: Not started
attendanceStates.help: No day opened yet, and the business day has not ended.

attendanceStates.label: Working
attendanceStates.help: Day is open and no break is running.

attendanceStates.label: On break
attendanceStates.help: A break is open inside an open day. Elapsed keeps counting; worked time does not.

attendanceStates.label: Day ended
attendanceStates.help: Closed. Worked and break totals are final.

attendanceStates.label: Absent
attendanceStates.help: DERIVED. No day opened and the business day is over. Never written — a member who is simply not in yet at 10am is Not started, not Absent.

attendanceStates.label: Unclosed
attendanceStates.help: DERIVED. Still open past the member's autoCloseAt. Contributes nothing to totals until a person resolves it. NOTHING AUTO-CLOSES: an auto-closed day is a number the system invented, an unclosed one is a question.

attendanceStates.label: On leave
attendanceStates.help: DERIVED. Approved leave covers the date and no day was opened. It suppresses Absent; it never writes an attendance row.

$comment_attendanceStates: `stored:false` is the whole point of this list. Absent and Unclosed are computed at read time against the member's own dayStartsAt / autoCloseAt and the payload's asOf. Storing them would need a sweep job, and this backend has no queue — only a 15-minute cron. The enquiries module withdrew its SLA sweep for exactly this reason.

lateRule.help: Late is computed AT OPEN against the member's own dayStartsAt plus graceMinutes, and stored on the row. Changing the policy later must not retroactively make last month late.

workKinds.label: Task
workKinds.help: A day's unit of work. Rolls up to a milestone.

workKinds.label: Milestone
workKinds.help: A dated commitment made of tasks. Progress is DERIVED from its children — completed ÷ total — and is never typed.

workKinds.label: Target
workKinds.help: A number to reach in a period. Progress accumulates from EOD deltas; it is the one kind whose progress a person writes.

workStatuses.label: Delay
workStatuses.help: DERIVED. dueDate < today on a non-terminal item. It is a column and a stage name, and it is stored nowhere.

$comment_workStatuses: FIVE STAGES, the same five for every member, and nobody can add a sixth. Four are stored; `delayed` is derived at read (dueDate < today AND not terminal) and takes precedence in the grouping, so an item is in exactly one column and the strip agrees with the board. A stored Delay would need a nightly sweep this backend has no queue for, and it would let a card read In progress three weeks past its date. BLOCKED IS NOT A STAGE any more: late is a date and waiting on someone is a relationship, so it moved to `blockedByItemId` plus a reason on the item.
$comment_workTransitions: Delay accepts no drop — there is nothing to write. Dragging OUT of it sets a stored stage, and the card leaves the column by itself once the date is met.

scopes.label: Only me
scopes.help: Always available, with no grant at all.

scopes.label: My reports
scopes.help: Members whose reportsTo points at the viewer. ONE LEVEL, not the transitive closure — a recursive default is a permission that silently widens every time somebody is hired.

scopes.label: Everyone
scopes.help: Full access, or the module's `all` verb.

$comment_scopes: TM-OD-01, answered 2026-08-30. Scoping is the API's job; the client renders what it is given and says which scope it is showing. A client-side filter over an unscoped payload is the same bug in a different place.

metricDefinitions.worked: Time between day open and day close, minus every closed break. An open day counts up to asOf; an unclosed one counts nothing.
metricDefinitions.late: First open later than the member's own dayStartsAt + graceMinutes. Stored at open.
metricDefinitions.absent: No day opened and the business day is over, on a configured working day.
metricDefinitions.onTimeRate: Days present and not late ÷ days present. Days absent are excluded — being away is not the same as being late, and averaging them together answers neither question.
metricDefinitions.completion: Work items completed ÷ items due, within the scope being shown. Never a per-person score.
metricDefinitions.planSubmitted: A DailyPlan exists for the member and business date with submittedAt set. A draft does not count.
metricDefinitions.eodSubmitted: A DailyReport exists for the member and business date with submittedAt set.

openDecisions.title: Scope
openDecisions.note: Senior sees their own reports, one level, plus an `all` verb for everyone.

openDecisions.title: Salary slips
openDecisions.note: Generated — by Finance. Team reads Payslip rows by memberId and never generates.

openDecisions.title: Working hours
openDecisions.note: Per member, defaulted from a company setting. The seed already varies them.

openDecisions.title: Calendar drag and drop
openDecisions.note: Recommended out of v1 — a silent drag leaves no reason.

openDecisions.title: Is EOD mandatory
openDecisions.note: Recommended no. It surfaces as missing; it never blocks. A forced report is a fabricated one.

openDecisions.title: Performance score
openDecisions.note: Recommended no. Show the numbers, sort by any column.

openDecisions.title: Leave and holidays
openDecisions.note: Out of v1. Absent is derived only on configured working days, and the week grid already skips Sat/Sun.

$comment_tagSuggestions: STATIC COPY, and only suggestions. A tag itself is a RECORD owned by the member who typed it — src/content/team/tags.json — so two members may both hold `call` and neither can rename the other's. Any tag, fixed stages: a tag is one person's way of finding their own work, a stage is how the company reads everybody's at once.
$comment_leave: Approved leave SUPPRESSES a derived absence. It never writes an attendance row — two records answering 'was this person in' would disagree inside a month.
$comment_documents: TWO BUCKETS, NOT ONE. An Agreement travels company → member and is frozen at send; a Resource travels member → company and the member may delete it. They differ in direction, permission and retention, which is why one tab holds two lists rather than one list holding both.
